rules.title: Statewide Rent Increase Cap (Initiative Petition, Ch. 40P)
rules.requirement: This proposed state law would cap annual rent increases for most residential units in Massachusetts at the lower of the CPI increase or 5% in any 12-month period, regardless of tenant turnover. A base rent is set from the amount charged on January 31, 2026 (or last charged rent if vacant, or first rent charged after adoption if none).
rules.key_value: CPI increase or 5%, whichever is lower, per 12-month period

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to all leased residential dwelling units in the commonwealth except specified exemptions; voucher tenancy does not count as being 'regulated by a public authority.'

rules.exemptions: Exempt: dwelling units in owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; units whose rents are regulated by a public authority (mobile housing voucher tenancy does not count); units rented primarily to transient guests for less than 14 consecutive days; units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes; units whose first certificate of occupancy is less than 10 years old, for 10 years from issuance. Exempt units must receive a written notice of exemption with the lease or, if no lease, before acceptance of the first rent payment.
rules.interaction: Section 5 states nothing in the chapter interferes with existing tenant rights/protections under current state or federal law.
rules.penalty: Violations are deemed unfair and deceptive acts under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93A; tenants may sue under ch. 93A § 9, and the Attorney General may bring an enforcement action under ch. 93A § 4 seeking restitution, civil penalties, and injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: This chapter shall establish a limit on any annual rent increase for a covered dwelling unit in the commonwealth, which shall not exceed the annual increase in Consumer Price Index or 5%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period.
rules.conflict_note: This is a ballot initiative petition (25-21) that has not yet been enacted as of the query date; it would need voter approval to take effect.
